title: Warm-Start Iterative QITE for Distribution Network Reconfiguration via Branch-Exchange Encoding
authors: Noah Crum, Pete Pritchard, Tanner Rase, Phillip C. Lotshaw, Shaked Regev, Claudio Girotto, Ananth Kaushik, Paul Smith
abstract: We present a hybrid quantum-classical algorithm for distribution network reconfiguration, a combinatorial optimization problem on power distribution networks, that combines a radiality preserving branch-exchange encoding with iterative warm-start quantum imaginary-time evolution to minimize active line losses. The encoding uses a fixed-width binary representation of sequential branch-exchange actions, ensuring that every register outcome decodes to a radial configuration. The quantum subroutine is informed by a surrogate model fit to classically-solved alternating current power flow (ACPF) labels. After a set budget of ACPF solves and circuit samples is exhausted, the algorithm returns the lowest-loss configuration seen. We employ our algorithm on ten test cases, including seven commonly-used benchmark cases and three cases we modified from these and similar standard systems. We include two methods to reduce problem size, which enable extensions of the algorithm to larger networks. We successfully reach minimal-loss configurations for six cases and find configurations with losses from 0.2 percent to 2.18 percent above the reported reference minimal loss for the other four.
summary: This paper presents a novel hybrid quantum-classical algorithm to solve the distribution network reconfiguration problem, aiming to minimize power line losses. It uses Iterative Quantum Imaginary-Time Evolution (QITE) guided by a surrogate model trained on classical power flow data. The method successfully finds near-optimal loss configurations across various test cases, demonstrating the potential of quantum computation for complex engineering optimization.
main_problem: The paper addresses the combinatorial optimization problem of finding the optimal radial configuration in an electrical distribution network that minimizes total active line losses.
main_result: The hybrid quantum-classical algorithm successfully reached minimal-loss configurations for six out of ten tested cases, achieving losses within 2.18% of the reference minimum for the remaining four.
method: It employs a hybrid approach combining Iterative Quantum Imaginary-Time Evolution (QITE) with a surrogate model trained on classical Active Current Power Flow (ACPF) results to guide quantum sampling.
model_or_system: The system is an electrical power distribution network, modeled using a branch-exchange encoding to represent switch configurations. The optimization objective is minimizing active line losses, $L(z)$.

main_assumptions: The algorithm assumes the branch-exchange encoding covers all radial topologies, and the QITE update is an approximation of the true imaginary-time evolution.

paper_structure: The paper details the formulation of the DNR problem, introduces the branch-exchange encoding, develops the surrogate model fitting procedure, and finally derives the specific finite QITE update rule necessary for the iterative quantum optimization process.
why_interesting: The core methodology—using quantum imaginary-time evolution guided by a classical surrogate model to solve a complex combinatorial optimization problem—is a direct application of quantum algorithms to a real-world engineering challenge, relevant to quantum computation applications.
